applicable_when: The kernel fuses a convolution bias-add with a strided store: input is channel-last with stride-256 in the channel dim, but output has stride-512 (double). The store out_ptr0 + (x0 + 512*x1) where x0=xindex%256, x1=xindex//256 scatters writes with a 2x stride gap, causing non-coalesced L1TEX transactions and 13.7-cycle stalls (56.9% of all cycles). With XBLOCK=128 the grid is 3920 blocks on 132 SMs, producing a 1808-block partial wave (50% tail overhead). Three prior attempts to fix this by simply increasing XBLOCK all failed correctness (max_diff ~8.0) because the index decomposition x0=xindex%256 and x1=xindex//256 is only correct when XBLOCK divides evenly into the 256-element channel dimension. The correct fix is to rewrite the kernel with an explicit 2D grid: one dimension iterates over the 256 channels (x0), the other over the N*H*W spatial positions (x1=501760//256=1960). This makes the index arithmetic exact and independent of XBLOCK, then @triton.autotune can safely explore XBLOCK values without correctness risk.
